messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - Dedicated pool 'dedicated-enterprise-zenith' reports GPU capacity exhaustion. All 8 GPUs at 100%, pending queue increasing. Affected tenant: zenith-inc (tenant_id: zen-9012). Autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool_max_instances=8. Paging: @Jamal (SRE) @Aisha (Platform) @Priya (CS). Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-capacity

Jamal (SRE): On it. I'm checking pool status and autoscaler logs. Jamal (SRE) is assuming incident lead.

Aisha (Platform): seeing the same in dashboards — queue latency spike to 450ms p95 and token backlog for that tenant only. scale_policy for that pool has allow_burst=false and max_instances=8. No recent config changes.

Olivia (Runtime): quick thought — can we fall back that tenant to a lighter model variant (quantized/4-bit) while we recover? That would reduce per-request GPU time. Also check KV cache hit rate for that tenant; if cache is cold it could exacerbate.

Tim (Infra): i can check cloud quotas. If pool max is hitting cloud quota for GPUs, we might be able to use preemptible burst nodes temporarily. Give me a sec to confirm availability in the region.

Jamal (SRE): running diagnostics commands now:
```
# inspect pool
redwoodctl pools describe dedicated-enterprise-zenith --output json | jq '.status'
# tail autoscaler logs
redwoodctl logs autoscaler --pool dedicated-enterprise-zenith --since 15m | tail -n 200
```

Jamal (SRE): autoscaler logs show: "scale_up blocked: reached pool_max_instances". No errors from cloud provider in logs.

Leo (Eng): can we route zenith-inc to a fallback dedicated pool (shared-dedicated-fallback) while we add capacity? Routing policy supports per-tenant overrides but needs a rollout. That would require short DNS/Routing change and CS approval.

Priya (CS): flagging customer impact: zenith-inc reporting timeouts from internal app monitoring. Their SLAs are impacted for inference calls. I'm drafting a message to their ops with ETA of ~15-30m while we add capacity. Need clear mitigation steps to include in the message.

Aisha (Platform): cloud quota for GPUs in us-west-2 shows spare 4 preemptible GPUs. We can enable burst (preemptible) up to 4 with a short config change. The pool currently has allow_burst=false. If we set allow_burst=true and burst_limit=4, autoscaler should be able to add them automatically.

Tim (Infra): confirmed: provider permits 4 additional preemptible GPUs in the region. Might see node churn, but it's acceptable as an emergency measure.

Jamal (SRE): proposal: enable allow_burst=true and burst_limit=4 on dedicated-enterprise-zenith, reduce per-request concurrency for zenith-inc to lower KV/cache pressure, and concurrently failover lower-priority tenants if needed. Approve?

Priya (CS): approved. I'll send the customer note once we have a mitigation in place. Draft: "We've detected heavy utilization and are enabling burst capacity; expected restoration within 15 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and postmortem"

Olivia (Runtime): also pushing a temporary policy to route zenith-inc requests to model-variant: compact-1 for non-critical endpoints. I'll add a header-based override in the routing rules for that tenant for 20m.

Jamal (SRE): applying emergency change now:
```
# enable burst on the pool
redwoodctl pool update --name dedicated-enterprise-zenith --set allow_burst=true --set burst_limit=4
# throttle tenant concurrency
redwoodctl tenants update zen-9012 --set max_concurrency=4
```

Jamal (SRE): change applied. Autoscaler metric shows nodes requested. Waiting for nodes to join.

incident-bot: Update - 2 new preemptible nodes provisioning, expected join in ~2-4 minutes.

Tim (Infra): provider console shows 2/4 preemptible nodes active, 2 still provisioning. No quota errors now.

Olivia (Runtime): routing override pushed for zen-9012 to model-variant compact-1 for non-critical routes. Hit rate to compact-1 is ~40% now. That should drop GPU time per request by ~35%.

Priya (CS): sent interim status to zenith-inc: "We've enabled emergency burst and routing changes to reduce load; our estimate to restored normal service is 20 minutes. We'll follow up with details and timeline." They replied: "Thanks, please keep us updated. This is impacting internal dashboards."

Jamal (SRE): metrics look good — queue length decreasing, p95 latency trending down to baseline. Confirmed all tenant requests being served. Marking incident as mitigated.

Aisha (Platform): let's keep allow_burst=true for now but lower burst_limit to 2 and monitor for 1 hour. We'll open a ticket with cloud provider to increase quota and adjust pool_max_instances to 12 for this tenant after approval.

Tim (Infra): opened provider support ticket #SUP-10482 requesting permanent quota increase for GPUs in us-west-2. ETA from provider ~24-48h.

Jamal (SRE): post-incident actions (assigned):
- Aisha: update pool policy to allow controlled burst and set alerts for pool_max hit (P0 -> P1).
- Olivia: automated fallback policy to route to compact variants when per-tenant queue > 200ms for 3m.
- Tim: follow up with provider on quota ticket.
- Priya: customer follow-up and timeline to zenith-inc and legal if needed.
- Jamal: write incident timeline and impact summary for postmortem.

Leo (Eng): we should also add a test in our chaos suite to simulate dedicated-tenant spike and verify burst path works end-to-end. I'll file an RFC.

Priya (CS): zenith-inc acknowledged mitigation and asked for a postmortem. They're especially concerned about whether this can happen again during monthly reporting spikes. I set an action item to discuss rate-limiting and plan for scheduled reports.

Jamal (SRE): handoff: I'll be primary for the postmortem write-up. Ops on-call in 30m will take any follow-ups — tagging @Aisha for next 30m watch. If anything regresses, page SREs.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration: ~16 minutes from page to mitigation. SLA impact: zenith-inc experienced elevated latency and partial timeouts for ~12 minutes.

Jamal (SRE): closing thread for now. Will open postmortem doc and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:"
